issues.detail: The Greek 'πασα βασιλεια' (every kingdom) is translated as 'Nước nào' (any/which kingdom). The Greek expresses a universal statement about all kingdoms, whereas the Vietnamese phrasing suggests a conditional or specific 'any' kingdom.

The Greek 'εφ εαυτην διαμερισθεισα' (divided against itself) is rendered as 'tự chia rẽ nhau' (divided among themselves/each other). The Greek emphasizes internal division within a single entity, while the Vietnamese implies division between multiple entities.
